transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Um... well, I was mostly told to come in. By my wife, and my director at work. 

They think I... I guess they think I can't seem to stop launching projects. Just... doing a lot. Work plans, setting up new certification schedules, tearing apart the home network to upgrade it... messaging a bunch of old contacts. I don't know. I guess it gets pretty intense, and I just kind of... blow past normal limits. Until my wife or my boss has to step in and tell me to stop. So... that's why I'm here.
Do you often feel unusually happy or excited when you're launching these projects?

Um... I guess you could say that. Some weeks I just feel... I don't know, almost electric. Like I'm unstoppable. 

But... I wouldn't always call it happy. If there's even a tiny delay with something, or... if my wife asks a question about what I'm doing, I tend to snap. It just... it feels like everyone is trying to slow me down on purpose.
Have you experienced periods where you felt sad or empty for most of the day?

Yeah... sometimes. 

There are stretches where I just... I wake up feeling like a failed version of myself. It's just heavy. Flat. During those times, even answering my wife's normal questions feels like too much. So... yeah. I guess I do get like that.
How long do these periods of feeling electric and unstoppable usually last?

Um... I don't really track them day by day. But... these stretches, where I'm just really driven and... I guess overconfident, barely sleeping... they've been happening for a while now. Roughly a year and eight months, I think.
Do you notice that your periods of feeling electric and unstoppable are usually followed by periods of feeling sad or empty?

I guess... yeah, sometimes one follows the other. I don't know the exact pattern. But if I had to add up all those... those low times, the times I just withdraw... it's probably been about seven months total, out of this whole time.
Do you usually return to a normal mood between these periods of feeling electric and unstoppable and the periods of feeling sad or empty?

I suppose so, yes. There are... stretches where things feel calm, or just flat. Sometimes for a few weeks. I'm not really up, and I'm not down either. But... I still notice things. Like the Microsoft Teams statuses at work... I still know they're coded warnings. And I still hear... brief comments sometimes, even when I'm alone. So my mood is normal, I guess, but... those other things don't stop.
Do you feel like you switch between these different states, like being electric and unstoppable is a distinct state from your normal self?

I guess so. It's... a different gear, yeah. 

Some weeks I have that electric feeling, like I'm just unstoppable. But... it's not always a good thing. If there's a tiny delay with something, or... if my wife just asks me a simple question, I tend to snap. It just feels like... I don't know, like everyone is doing it on purpose just to slow me down.
How long do these electric and unstoppable periods typically last, is it usually just a few days or can they last for several days at a time?

I don't really count the exact days. It's... hard to keep track of it like that. But... those stretches, where I'm just really driven and don't sleep much... they've been a part of my life for roughly a year and eight months now. I just know it's been going on for about that long.
Do you feel like you're fully back to your normal self between these electric periods?

Not always. I mean... there are other stretches. Where I just wake up feeling... heavy. Flat. Like a failed version of myself, I guess. When it's like that... even just answering my wife's normal questions feels like it's too much. So... no. Not always my normal self.
Do you usually crash or feel extremely tired after one of these electric and unstoppable periods?

Not really. I mean... I don't usually feel tired. There are runs where I sleep... maybe three hours. I'll wake up sharp at 3 or 4 a.m. and... it just feels like I've been handed bonus time, I guess. So... no, not really tired.
Do you hear those brief comments when you're in your normal mood, or is it mostly when you're feeling electric or feeling down?

I hear them... at other times too. Even when I'm not feeling electric or... heavy. There have been stretches, maybe a few weeks at a time, where my mood was just... flat. Normal, I guess. But... I still heard the comments. And... I still knew the Teams statuses at work were coded warnings. So, it's not just when my mood is up or down.
Do you feel like these electric periods come on suddenly, or do they build up gradually?
I'm... not really sure. I haven't really paid attention to how it starts. It just... kind of happens, I guess. I don't really track it.
Do you feel like you're switching into a different mode of yourself when you become electric and unstoppable?

I guess you could say that. I just... I feel electric, like I said. Unstoppable. But... it's also... I don't know. If there's a delay, or if my wife just asks a simple question, I... I snap. It just feels like everyone is intentionally trying to slow me down.
Do you feel like you're fully in your electric and unstoppable state from the moment it starts, or is there a buildup to it?
I don't know. Like I said, I don't really track how it starts. I just... notice it when I'm already in it, I guess. I haven't really thought about a buildup.
How many days at a time do you typically feel electric and unstoppable?
I don't really count the days. It's usually... some weeks. I'll just have weeks where I feel like that, until... well, like I said, until I end up snapping at my wife over something small.
Do you feel like you're back to your normal self right before one of these electric periods starts?

I guess... yeah. There are stretches where I'm not electric, and I'm not... down. Just flat, for a few weeks. But... I mean, even then, I still know about the coded warnings in the Teams statuses at work. And I still... hear those brief comments sometimes, when no one's in the room. So... I don't know what normal is, really.
Do you feel like you're switching into a completely different state of yourself when you become electric and unstoppable, compared to your normal self or when you're feeling down?

I don't know if I'd call it a completely different state. It's just... like I said, I have those weeks where I feel almost electric. Unstoppable. But then... I don't know. If there's a tiny delay, or my wife just asks a simple question... I snap. It just starts to feel like... like everyone is trying to slow me down on purpose. So... yeah, I guess it's different.
Do you feel like you're fully back to your normal self between each of these electric periods?

I don't know... not always. Like I said before, sometimes I'm just flat. But... there are also stretches where I wake up and just feel... heavy. Like a failed version of myself, I guess. 

It's hard to explain. Just... really heavy and flat. During those times, even... even just answering my wife's normal questions feels like it's too much. So... no, I wouldn't call that normal.
Do you feel like you're switching into a completely different state of yourself when you become electric and unstoppable?

I... thought I just answered that. I don't really know about a different state. 

It's just... like I said, some weeks I feel electric and unstoppable. But then... there's a tiny delay, or my wife asks a question, and I snap. It just feels like everyone is trying to slow me down on purpose. I don't really have another way to describe it.
Do your electric and unstoppable periods usually last at least four consecutive days?
I guess so. I don't really track the days. It just... it lasts a while. Maybe a few days, maybe longer. I'm not really sure.
